nodes.summary: A class of groups is a property of groups: for each group $G$ it gives a proposition, read as "$G$ belongs to the class". No closure under isomorphism is required.
nodes.title: Classes of groups

nodes.title: Skiba's theorem (Kourovka Problem 11.91)

nodes.summary: The statement that every hereditary formation $\mathfrak F$ of finite soluble groups such that every finite soluble non-simple minimal non-$\mathfrak F$-group (a group outside $\mathfrak F$ all of whose proper subgroups lie in $\mathfrak F$) is a Shmidt group is saturated, that is, every finite soluble group $G$ whose quotient $G/\Phi(G)$ by its Frattini subgroup $\Phi(G)$ lies in $\mathfrak F$ itself lies in…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.91 (statement)

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak F$ of groups is a hereditary formation of finite soluble groups if every group in $\mathfrak F$ is finite and soluble; $\mathfrak F$ is closed under isomorphisms, under taking subgroups and under taking quotients by normal subgroups; and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $M$ and $N$ such that $G/M$ and $G/N$ lie in $\mathfrak F$, also $G/(M \cap N)$ lies in $\mathfrak F$.
nodes.title: Hereditary formations of finite soluble groups

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak F$ be a class of groups. A group $G$ is a minimal non-$\mathfrak F$-group if $G$ does not lie in $\mathfrak F$ but every proper subgroup of $G$ lies in $\mathfrak F$.
nodes.title: Minimal non-members of a class of groups

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak F$ of groups is saturated if every finite soluble group $G$ such that $G/\Phi(G)$ lies in $\mathfrak F$, where $\Phi(G)$ is the Frattini subgroup of $G$, itself lies in $\mathfrak F$.
nodes.title: Saturated classes of groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a Shmidt group if it is finite and not nilpotent, but every proper subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Shmidt groups

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
